stops.note: close-fitting tartan leg-wear of the Highlands (Irish triús); its deeper origin is uncertain
after Culloden, the Dress Act of 1746 banned Highland dress, trews and kilts included, until its repeal in 1782
the -ers ending copies 'drawers'; long trousers pushed out knee breeches in men's fashion in the Regency years around the 1810s

current_meaning: an outer garment covering each leg separately from waist to ankle
